title: iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB Cosmic Orange – AU Stock – $1,960 @ Skytree
body:
Deal: iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB Cosmic Orange – AU Stock – $1,960 @ Skytree

[spc12go] They will not match sky tree. I was at a store earlier today and they said this. “Sky tree is not a real website it’s a fake website”, I told them there’s a physical store in Queensland. Then they claim “we got a memo from HQ not to match sky tree, our price matching team placed an order and it never arrived”. I pointed to their policy it says as long as the item has the same model number which they do, then they said this “they mentioned 24 months warranty which means it’s a fake website as Apple only carry 12 months warranty”
Hope you guys have better luck.
[Lizard Spock] our price matching team placed an order and it never arrived
So that's how they test the legitimacy of each store? Sounds like they just want to weasel out of a price beat.
[CrikeyCheap] My Officeworks Price Beat experience
I’ve successfully had Officeworks price beat a similar previous deal at my local store.
On the first attempt, one of the team members declined the Price Beat. I went back the following morning and tried again with another staff member, and the Price Beat was approved without any issues.
So based on my experience, I wouldn’t assume that a refusal from one staff member necessarily means the deal is ineligible. It may be worth trying again or speaking with another team member/manager, provided the deal meets the published Price Beat requirements.
[jv] provided the deal meets the published Price Beat requirements.
That's the key here…
Might be worth raising an ACCC complaint for OW misleading advertising …
[jv] they mentioned 24 months warranty which means it’s a fake
Apple website say 2 years for warranty…
https://www.apple.com/legal/warranty/docs/statutory_warranty…
[tonester] Apple Limited Warranty
2 years from date of purchase for Apple Watch Edition
1 year from date of purchase for all other Apple products
[jv] Without limiting consumers rights, Apple will provide its own remedies equivalent to those remedies in the consumer guarantee provisions of the Australian Consumer Law at any time within 24 months of the date of purchase . For the avoidance of doubt, Apple acknowledges that the Australian Consumer Law may provide for remedies beyond 24 months for a number of its products.
